transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I keep seeing that explosion in my head like it’s happening all over again, and I can’t shut it off. It was a really bad accident at work about a year ago, and it just won't stop playing in my mind.
When you experience these flashbacks, do you feel as though you are physically back in the moment of the accident, or are you fully aware that you are in the present time?

For a few seconds, I really do feel like I'm physically back in that basement and I completely lose track of where I actually am. I can smell the gas and smoke and hear him screaming, whether I'm at work or just standing in the grocery store. It's like the real world just vanishes until it passes.
Do you find yourself actively avoiding places, people, or activities that remind you of the accident to prevent these flashbacks from happening?

Yeah, I do everything I can to avoid them. I’ll drive the long way around just to stay away from older buildings or that side of town, and if anyone at church brings up the accident or asks about apprentices, I just shut down and walk away. I just can't stand having all those feelings come back up.
Since the accident, have you noticed that you are more easily startled, or do you find yourself constantly on edge and scanning your surroundings for danger?

Yes, I am incredibly jumpy now. If someone drops a tool on the job or slams a car door behind me, I jump out of my skin and my heart starts pounding like crazy. It takes me a really long time to stop shaking, even after I realize everything is actually fine.
